content.thinking:
I'll write the whole scene file carefully in one pass to avoid API errors - designing a Genshin-style alchemy workbench, roughly 1.6m wide, with cel-shaded paints, gold trim, glowing potions in a teal/cream/gold palette, plus maybe a low shelf behind it to add depth without overcomplicating the scene.

Checking the builder API conventions for parts, lathes, extrusions, and textures, I'm planning the potion flasks as opaque glass-colored bodies with glowing liquid, gold bands, and corks since true transparency isn't available - staying mindful of the flat color limit by leaning on cel-paint materials where possible.

For the table I'm sketching out dimensions: a wooden top around 1.6 x 0.06 x 0.7 at y≈0.9, four legs, and a grain-textured paint for the wood wrapped in cel for proper lighting. I'm planning helper functions for boxes and cylinders built from part geometry, then laying out the full scene list starting with the table (top, gold trim apron, legs, lower shelf, crossbar, drawer fronts with brass knobs) before adding a back shelf rack with jars and herb bundles reaching up to about 1.55 in height.

Next I'm detailing the books: a stack of four with painted covers, cream page edges, gold spine bands and a clasp, plus an open book up front rendered with angled page planes carrying a rune-like texture, tuning the plane's up-vector so the illustration faces away from the viewer correctly. Then I'm moving on to a brass balance scale with a lathed base, pillar rod, beam, and two hanging pans.

Now I'm planning the potions as flasks of varied shapes -- round-bottom, conical Erlenmeyer, tall vial, hex bottle -- glowing in Genshin-style elemental colors (pyro, hydro, dendro, electro, anemo, cryo), plus a mortar and pestle with green herbal paste, and herb elements as hanging bundles and potted plants using leaf-textured cards. Next I'll work out the candle or lantern piece.

I'll only put labels on cylindrical vials to avoid floating decals on tapered flasks, then define a helper function for building potions in world coordinates with position, kind, and color as parameters.

For round flask kinds, I'm sketching the liquid sphere, neck cylinder, cork, and gold collar, plus a small highlight sphere for glass shine.

Now for the Erlenmeyer flask I'm defining lathe outlines for the glowing liquid section and the pale glass neck above it as separate solids...

For the other containers, I'm sketching out a vial with a cork cap and label, and a hexagonal bottle with a shoulder cone, neck, and gold stopper sphere, then planning a switch function keyed by container kind to generate each shape.

Now I'm designing the hanging herb rack: posts and a top beam with shelves, bundles of herbs tied with stems pointing down, and leaning cards using leaf textures, pulling in the `frame` helper for orientation.

For each bundle, I'm adding a knot sphere, rod stems extending downward at slight angles, and small leaf cards clustered along the lower stem to look like hanging foliage.

For the potted plants, I'm building a lathe terracotta pot with a gold band, a soil disc, and a ring of upright leaf cards flaring outward from the center using manually computed direction vectors per index.

Writing leaf SVG texture...

Now I'm designing the page and label textures, then building the open book model with a cover, slightly tilted pages, and texture planes on top.

Still defining book geometry...

I'll add a helper function to convert local coordinates into world coordinates using a Y-axis rotation, so book parts can be placed and rotated as a group with simple degree-based rotation values. Then I'm working out the trig for rotating points around Y and starting on the lathe geometry for the brass piece.

Still writing lathe profiles...

Now I'm placing the gem in one pan and weights in the other, keeping both level. Then I'm working out positions for the scales and alembic setup on the tabletop, planning the burner, flask, tubing, and tripod rods while watching for spacing conflicts with other items.

Still placing scene elements... I'm figuring out the arcing tube connecting the alembic flask to a receiver vessel, then laying out the potions row with flasks on the back right and a stack of books plus a scroll toward the right side of the table.

Now I'm working out positions for the mortar with herbs, a potted plant, loose herb sprigs, and cards on the table front, plus a candle on the book stack. I'm adjusting the crystal cluster placement to avoid overlapping with the inkwell, quill, and book stack, nudging the stack and ink items slightly right to make room.

Then I'm placing the back rack: posts at the table edges, a shelf at a given height with jars, checking that potion flasks on the back row clear the posts and shelf board, and sketching an upper shelf higher up.

I need to make sure the hanging herb bundles from the beam and the items on the shelf don't collide vertically or horizontally, so I'm adjusting the beam height and staggering x-positions between bundles and shelf items to keep clearance.

I also want to add a glowing lantern hanging from the center of the beam, giving it gold lathe caps and a glass box for that warm glow — need to check its drop height doesn't clash with shelf items near x=0 either.

Now I'm shaping the rack posts with gold-capped spheres rising from table top to the top shelf, adding diagonal cross braces for support between posts and shelf ends, and skipping the back panel. For the lower shelf, I'm populating it with a slatted wooden crate, a cloth-tied burlap sack, a bucket, and a large jug to fill the space beneath.

Moving up to the drawer apron, I'm placing two drawer faces with brass knobs and gold keyhole plates on the front panel, then building the tapered legs from floor to seat height with small gold-capped feet and matching side aprons. For the tabletop itself, I'm sizing a slab with wood-grain coloring and adding thin gold trim strips around its edges.

For the surface decoration, I'm adding a decorative runner cloth across the front center with a teal-and-gold pattern and tassels, positioning it carefully so it doesn't overlap the open book or inkwell while sitting just above the tabletop to avoid z-fighting.

I also want to add gold filigree tassel cards leaning against the shelf edge and table apron ends for that Genshin-style elemental glow aesthetic.

I'm keeping part and triangle counts in check by minimizing segments, and defining gold cel-shaded materials with a lighter base and darker shadow tone for the painted trim, while reserving flat emissive colors for any glow elements.

Now I'm working through the material palette for the wood and cloth parts, pairing grain textures with explicit shadow colors to keep the cel shading consistent rather than relying on uncertain auto-derived shadows.

Still defining more colors...

Still writing type helpers...

Now I'm sketching the table geometry with a wood top, darker apron, and legs positioned at each corner.

Adding knobs, keyhole plates, and gold backing panels behind each drawer front, then checking the depth alignment against the apron face. I'm also placing a thin gold inlay strip along the top edge and corner studs, plus starting on a runner texture for the surface.

Still modeling the burner geometry...

Still working out tube geometry...I'm connecting a pale glass tube via bezier sweep from the flask to the erlenmeyer receiver, then shaping the mortar as a lathe profile with a concave stone outline.

Now I'm adding the paste-filled interior with a greenish disc at the right radius and height, then placing a tilted pestle rod with rounded stone caps and some flat leaning herb leaves around the mortar.

For the potted plant, I'm lathing the pot's silhouette with a flared rim and interior cavity, then figuring out how to add a gold band near the top using a thin torus scaled to the pot's radius at that height.

I'm also planning the plant itself: ten leaf cards leaning outward in a ring from a central soil cylinder, plus a few stems rising up with small glowing flower clusters in pink and gold tones to add life on top.

Now I'm sketching the book stack prop—four books of varying heights and sizes stacked at an angle, topped with a pale wax candle with a drip and a glowing flame spike. Next to it I'm designing an inkwell as a lathed dark-glass shape with a gold lid, paired with a quill made from a thin cream rod angled upward from the inkwell.

For the feather vane, I'm weighing options—texture cards versus a proper extruded leaf-shaped outline oriented along the quill's slanted direction, working out the right axis vectors so the shape doesn't collapse.

Defining feather outline points...

I'm scaling the vane shorter with teal-white coloring, then working on placing a rolled scroll cylinder with the right rotation to lie flat.

Now I'm adding the parchment scroll with wooden knob ends and a red ribbon torus wrapped around its middle, then checking positions so it doesn't overlap the inkwell or crystal stack nearby.

For the glowing crystal cluster, I'm placing five tilted spikes with hexagonal cross-sections in cyan tones, rising from a small dodecahedron base rock.

Now I'm laying out the potions row along z=-0.2, checking collisions with the book stack: a round violet flask, cyan vial, amber hex bottle, pink erlenmeyer, and green vial, nudging x positions so nothing overlaps the stack's back edge.

I also want a small test tube rack near the front-left, made from a wooden base plank with holes and side posts holding the tubes upright, sized so the tubes clear the shelf board above.

Each tube has a glowing colored liquid layer in the lower half and pale glass in the upper half, held between two horizontal rack planks with posts at the ends. I'm checking placement coordinates so the rack doesn't collide with the alembic, mortar and pestle, or the open book nearby.

For the shelf, I'm skipping loose herb sprigs and instead planning five lathe-shaped jars with pale glass bodies and gold lids, each filled with a different colored content — dried green herbs, red mushroom bits, glowing blue lumps — to vary the row visually.

I'm also adding a leaning cluster of upright books with gold-banded spines and a tall bottle alongside them to fill out the shelf composition.

I'm planning the full shelf layout now: upright books on the left, jars spaced across the middle, and a decanter with a round flask on the right, leaving clearance for hanging bundles above. I'm also sketching small tassel ornaments as gold-corded, teal-fringed decorations to hang from the shelf edge and table corners.

I'm now positioning hanging elements near the drawer knobs and table apron corners, double-checking their coordinates so they clear the tabletop edges, and starting to place a lantern hanging from the overhead beam with a chain or rod connecting it.

I'm detailing the lantern's parts next -- a glowing glass box, gold base and cap, a lathe-shaped top cone, and a ring near the attachment point -- while checking that its lowest point doesn't collide with the shelf jars below, then beginning to add the four corner support posts.

I'll skip the back panel for simplicity, and instead focus on hanging bundles tied to the beam at four symmetric x-positions, each attached via a short tie rod near the top.

Each bundle gets five splayed stems dropping down in green, decorated with leaf-and-flower card frames placed at varying heights, cross-faced and randomly textured for variety, plus a small colored ribbon accent near the tie point.

Now I'm adding storage under the table—a wooden crate with corner posts and slats, potions resting on the lower shelf, and a cloth sack built from a lathe profile for soft rounded sides.

Still refining the jug shape and handle geometry...

Checking the gold post caps come out around 1.83 total, fine. I'm defining wood grain axes for boards versus legs, adding small white highlight spheres to the potion sticks, planning simple label textures for vials and jars, and writing a helper function to generate different potion shapes by kind and color.

Still writing potion geometry...

Working out cylinder vertex placement so the label plane sits flush against the flat face at the correct radius and orientation. For the hexagonal vial, I'm defining the liquid, shoulder, neck cylinders with 6-sided geometry plus a gold stopper ball on top.

I still need to size the gold band to match the taper between body and neck, and decide on glass coloring using a pale cel gradient. For candles I'll just stack cylinder segments, and for cards/frames I need to check the `frame(at, axis)` signature and how `b.cards()` accepts texture arrays before writing that code.

I'm also planning the loose sprigs in the mortar, leaning outward from the center, and sketching a `tor` ring helper for rotated torus shapes. Writing the texture SVGs...

Setting up two distinct page textures for left and right pages, then working out the open book geometry — spine hump, cover box dimensions, and the two paper blocks positioned symmetrically around the center spine.

Now I'm working out the scale placement, adjusting the beam length and pan radius so they don't collide with the burner or overhang the table edge, settling on a shorter beam half-length with pans positioned closer to center.

Shifting attention to the alembic, receiver flask, and potion bottles, I'm nudging their x-coordinates to avoid overlaps, then checking the mortar and pestle against the nearby potted plant for spacing.

For the scale, I'm defining the pillar's cross-section profile with a tapered base, then placing the balance beam on top with hanging chains leading down to the pans at three angles.

Each pan gets a lathe outline for its rim and bowl shape, with a glowing dodecahedron gem in the left pan and a stack of gold cylinder weights in the right pan to keep things balanced visually despite the gem's heft. I'm also tossing in a few extra loose weights near the base of the scale for detail.

I'm keeping the code strict about types -- no `any`, no stray unused variables -- and importing a `frame` helper that takes a position and direction vector. I'm defining a position type alias and a small helper for building part options with optional rotation, then starting on a `book` function that takes offset coordinates, yaw, dimensions, cover/band colors, and an upright flag.

Now I'm writing a local-to-world coordinate transform that rotates points by the yaw angle, and sketching out how the cover box and pages box should be sized and offset so the pages peek out slightly from the closed cover on the fore-edge and top/bottom sides.

Adding spine bands and title plate...

Writing shelf book geometry...

Now I'm planning a candle sitting on top of the book stack with a gold holder, cream wax cylinder, drips, and a glowing flame cone, plus considering adding a subtle glowing rune ring motif nearby.

Skipping the extra teal glow accents to keep things simple, I'm now setting up typed helper imports -- glow, cel, and INK utilities, plus the bezier path and sweep functions for building tube and frame geometry. Writing component code...
